Understanding Semantic HTML

By
Jane Doe
| Published March 15, 2024

Semantic HTML provides meaning to structure. Elements like HTML <article>, <section>, and <nav> describe their content's role on the page.

Why Semantic HTML Matters

Using the right elements improves accessibility, SEO, and code maintainability. Screen readers and search engines rely on semantic structure to understand page content.

Interactive Elements

Published March 16, 2024
What is details/summary?

The <details> element creates a disclosure widget. The <summary> element provides the clickable heading. Click to expand and collapse content.

Already open details

This details element starts in the open state. Users can still click the summary to collapse it.

Another collapsible section

Multiple details elements can exist on a page, each functioning independently.
